Maya (CS): Drafting the customer follow-up for yesterday's degraded embeddings/latency incident. Posting a short timeline + what we did, and suggested credit offer. Please review for accuracy and tone.

Jonah (Oncall): +1 on timeline, but we should call out the affected regions (us-west1, eu-west1). Also clarify that there was no data exfiltration.

Liam (SRE): Correct — impact window 2026-03-15 02:12–02:57 UTC. Root cause was a regression in the routing compiler that caused backlog on the dedicated autoscaler. We had cascading queue growth which triggered increased latencies and 503s for some customers on lower-tier routes.

Maya (CS): Great — adding region + no-data note. Proposed opening paragraph: "We’re sorry — on 2026-03-15 we experienced elevated latency and intermittent 503 responses for embeddings and generation in US-WEST1 and EU-WEST1. Impact lasted ~45 minutes. No customer data was exposed. Our team prioritized restoring traffic and then working the root cause and mitigations." Thoughts?

Erin (Account): Tone looks good. Can we offer a one-time invoice credit equivalent to 10% of March usage for impacted customers? Also need an internal note to Sales so they can pre-empt customer questions.

Jonah (Oncall): 10% sounds reasonable as a standard CS mitigation. From ops side: we applied a config rollback at 02:28 UTC which dropped queue depth by 70%, then applied a targeted autoscaler patch at 02:45 UTC to prevent re-queueing. Final verification finished at 02:57 UTC.

Maya (CS): Adding rollback + patch times. Here's the full draft we plan to send to customers — please check the factual bits, then I'll send and post the status page update.

Maya (CS): ```
Subject: Incident report — elevated latency & intermittent errors on 2026-03-15

Hi —
We’re sorry for the disruption on 2026-03-15 that caused elevated latency and occasional 503 responses for embeddings and text generation in US-WEST1 and EU-WEST1 between 02:12–02:57 UTC.

What happened
During a routing compiler change we rolled earlier in the day, a regression caused unexpected request fan-out and queue growth in our dedicated autoscaler. This led to increased latency and intermittent 503 responses for a subset of traffic.

What we did
- At 02:28 UTC we rolled back the compiler change, which immediately reduced queue growth.
- At 02:45 UTC we applied an autoscaler patch to hard-limit goroutine queueing and prevent re-queueing under the previous pattern.
- At 02:57 UTC we verified normal traffic and latency metrics in the affected regions.

Impact
A subset of requests in US-WEST1 and EU-WEST1 experienced elevated latency and some 503s for ~45 minutes. No customer data was exposed.

Next steps
- We've reverted the problematic compiler change and deployed an autoscaler fix.
- We'll add a pre-deploy canary that simulates high-fanout patterns for dedicated routing.
- We'll add an alert to catch queue depth growth before it affects tail latency.

Compensation
We’re offering a one-time 10% invoice credit for impacted accounts in the affected regions. If you believe you were impacted and would like the credit applied, reply to this email and include your account ID.

Questions?
You can reply to this message or reach out to your CS contact directly.

Thanks for your patience —
Maya (Redwood Customer Success)
```

Liam (SRE): Draft is factually accurate. Suggest swapping the order of "What we did" bullets so rollback appears first (already done), and add the verification signal names: `latency_p95_embedding`, `request_rate_503`.

Maya (CS): Added signal names. Updated compensation sentence to include timeline cutoff: "impacted between 02:12–02:57 UTC".

Erin (Account): Can we also include a short internal blurb for sales: "Key ask: proactively reach out to top 15 customers in eu/us and offer to walk through timeline + credit. Use standard 10% credit template."

Jonah (Oncall): Internal comms note: create a Zendesk macro and a short Sales/Support playbook: step 1 confirm account impacted via `request_rate_503` spikes, step 2 offer 10% credit, step 3 escalate to SRE if the customer reports residual errors.

Maya (CS): I'll send the customer message 10:00 PST and post the status page update after legal OK. Here's proposed status page copy (short):

IncidentBot: STATUSPAGE DRAFT: ```
Summary: Intermittent elevated latency and 503s for embeddings and generation in US-WEST1 and EU-WEST1 on 2026-03-15 02:12–02:57 UTC.
Current status: Resolved
Impact: Some requests experienced elevated latency and intermittent errors.
Next steps: Root cause identified; mitigations deployed; follow-up report sent to affected customers.
```

Liam (SRE): Good. Also include link to post-incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0315-routing-compiler.

Erin (Account): Approved from GTM side. I'll draft the Sales note and the Zendesk macro.

Maya (CS): Thanks team — finalizing and will send after legal review. Will post here once sent. :thumbsup:

Jonah (Oncall): One last ask — add a preventative action to the "Next steps": "automated preflight that runs a synthetic fanout test on each routing compile in staging and on a small canary pool in prod."

Maya (CS): Added. Final version queued for legal. Will update thread with send timestamp and a copy of official status page link once published.
